body:
Omar Khan: Hey team — started getting a ton of 429s from our payroll scheduler around 03:10 UTC. It hits a Redwood API route used to generate signed payslips. We haven’t changed jobs, same cron, same QPS. 80% of jobs started failing with 429. No Retry-After processed in our client logs. Any quick triage pointers?

Alyssa Reyes: sorry to hear that, Omar. do you have one example request id / headers? also are the failures across regions or single region?

Omar Khan: Single region (us-west-2). sample response from our worker logs: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 12 Mar 2033 03:11:08 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
Retry-After: 30
X-Request-ID: rwd-req-04f2a9
X-RateLimit-Limit: 600
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1678475468

{"error":"rate limit exceeded"}
```

No obvious client retries; our scheduler fires 120 jobs at once when backlog > 0.

Devon Li: ok that header snapshot is helpful. sounds like a burst hitting a per-minute quota (RPM) or per-minute token bucket. quick notes:
- X-RateLimit-Limit looks like a per-minute cap (600).
- Remaining 0 + Retry-After:30 lines up with short cooldown.
- If you fire 120 jobs in parallel and each calls the same endpoint (no shared idempotency), you'll burst through RPM quickly.

Devon Li: immediate mitigations we can push:
1) soft-cap client-side: add random jitter when scheduling to spread across the minute window (e.g., uniform(0, 45s)).
2) implement exponential backoff with jitter on 429 responses, honoring Retry-After when present.
3) add a short server-side retry queue or integrate with existing job queue to rate-limit outbound calls.

Julia Park: +1 on jitter. also ask: are you on Hosted or Dedicated? if Dedicated we can temporarily raise the route quota for this customer while you stabilize.

Omar Khan: Hosted. we don’t have ability to change route quotas. can you raise temporarily?

Julia Park: I can request an emergency quota bump for the route. need customer org id and approximate sustained TPS you expect for the next hour. also: can you attach a short repro script? devon suggested a quick stress script.

Omar Khan: org id: org-44321. repro below (bash) — this is what our scheduler equivalent does when backlog hits 100:

```
#!/bin/bash
for i in {1..120}; do
  curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/payments/send" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"job_id":"'$RANDOM'","user_id":"u'$RANDOM'"}' &
done
wait
```

Alyssa Reyes: perfect repro. that loop will burst concurrently. try one of two quick client fixes:
- serialize jobs at low concurrency `xargs -P 5` or
- add `sleep $(shuf -n1 -i0-45)` inside loop to randomize.

Devon Li: also logs we’d like from your side: a) request IDs for a 2–3 failing calls, b) full request headers (redact tokens), c) any retry logs. we’ll also check inbound RPM/TPM metrics on our side for your org.

RateBot: Incident created: #INC-2033-799 (auto-detected rate spike for org-44321). Channel: incidents. Assigned: eng-sre.

Devon Li: from infra — I pulled the minute-by-minute counters: at 03:10 the org made ~140 requests in a 10s window, minute total ~620 which exceeded 600 minute limit. The server enforced the per-minute token bucket and returned 429s.

Devon Li: suggested medium-term changes:
- Use idempotency keys and combine small jobs into batched requests when possible.
- Use per-customer queue with token bucket on client side to smooth peaks (leaky-bucket).
- If you need guaranteed throughput spikes, consider Redwood Dedicated or a reserved quota contract.

Omar Khan: can you do a temporary increase right now? payroll runs in 30 minutes and we need a short window to deploy fixes.

Julia Park: I submitted emergency quota change request (SUP-PRIO). Ops can bump route from 600 -> 1200 for 1 hour. pending approval from capacity team (~10–15 min). I’ll post when live.

Devon Li: while waiting, quick low-risk client patch to deploy in 5 mins: limit concurrency to 10 and add jitter. e.g.:

```
# use GNU parallel to run up to 10 concurrent and randomize start
seq 1 120 | parallel -j10 --delay 0.1 --keep-order 'sleep $((RANDOM%45)); curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/payments/send -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @payload.json'
```

Omar Khan: deploying that now. will report back in 20. thanks. :pray:

deploy-bot: Deployment started by Omar Khan — payroll-worker v2.3.1 -> prod (canary=20%).

Alyssa Reyes: follow-ups for post-mortem:
- capture a timeline of when jobs moved from success -> 429s
- include scheduler backlog size, concurrency config, and whether any new deployments coincided
- verify your client respects Retry-After and implements jittered backoff

Omar Khan: quick update — after reducing concurrency to 10+ jitter, error rate dropped to ~1.5% and Retry-After respected. thanks all.

Devon Li: we approved a short-term rate bump; capacity team confirmed the 1-hour bump is live (route increased to 1200/min). please still roll the client fix as permanent mitigation.

Julia Park: closing the emergency ticket; I’ll follow up with a small SOW if you want a longer-term reserved capacity discussion.

Omar Khan: would like a blurb we can share with our ops team explaining cause (scheduler burst -> per-minute RPM exhausted) and the fix (jitter + concurrency cap + honor Retry-After). can you draft?

Alyssa Reyes: sending a quick blurb below you can paste: 

"Root cause: concurrent scheduler jobs produced a high-volume burst that exhausted the per-minute request quota on the Redwood endpoint. This triggered 429 responses from Redwood's per-minute token-bucket rate limiter.

Immediate fixes applied: lowered local parallelism to 10, added random start jitter (0-45s), and implemented exponential backoff honoring the Retry-After header. Redwood temporarily increased the route quota for 1 hour to allow payroll to finish.

Long-term recommendations: batch small requests where possible, add idempotency to avoid duplicate work on retries, implement a client-side token bucket or per-customer queue to smooth bursts, and consider Dedicated/reserved capacity for predictable high-throughput windows."

Omar Khan: perfect — thanks everyone. closing thread after payroll completes. :white_check_mark:
